rule: Return-to-running ramp starts at 10-12 miles/week (10 mi is also the floor of the weekly cap).
summary: Return-to-run guidance is level IV evidence: start conservatively (often walk-run), progress volume before speed, and let symptoms during, after and the day after running steer progression, rather than a fixed starting mileage. Previous injury and restarting running are among the more consistent injury risk factors, which supports a cautious start for this athlete. 10-12 mi over 3 runs (~3-4 mi each) is a sensible start for a trained adult with an old, settled injury, but the number is untested; with no runs in the previous 30 days the spike cap does not apply, so the first week's single-run length rests on this rule and the pain rule alone.

sources.note: Scoping review (50 studies, level IV): individualised graded return, often walk-run, distance before speed, symptom-guided
Clinical commentary: start when pain-free in daily life; load must not provoke symptoms during/after/next day
Systematic review: previous injury (strong evidence) and, in men, restarting running raise injury risk
